covers: rtextures.c's LoadImageAnim and LoadImageAnimFromMemory on helix-formats' test GIFs as stb_image composites them: one frame of GIF87a, rectangles kept over the screen, disposal to the background and to the previous frame (the first frame's) with transparency over it, a background index past 0 under a first frame smaller than the screen, transparency in a global and a local table, interlaced rows, 256 colors of noise filling the LZW code table, a file PIL wrote, a file of no frames, a file broken after its first frame (its first frame, as stb keeps the frames before a break, for every load), a missing file; a PNG as one frame; a name and a type known only as the program runs; the bytes typed .gif, .GIF and .png; the first frame LoadImage and LoadImageFromMemory read of each test GIF (a name and a type known only as the program runs, a type .Gif raylib doesn't read, a PNG by a name and a type made as it runs among them) and LoadTexture makes (read back), and the font LoadFont reads from a GIF (makegif.py's three glyphs on a magenta key)
notes: Where raylib gives an image with no data (a missing file, a GIF of no frames), LoadImageAnimAsync fails, printed as 0 frames, and LoadImageAsync, LoadImageFromMemoryAsync and LoadTextureAsync fail, printed as none (raylib's texture of id 0). The PNG is RGBA: helix-ray's file images say PIXELFORMAT_UNCOMPRESSED_R8G8B8A8 whatever the file's channels.
